findings.title: Installer identity is not checked when creating the integration
findings.body: The new GitHub-user check only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. If Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation.dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately, and build_integration never reads github_authenticated_user. installation_id is taken from the query string ahead of pipeline state, and the row is then created with the app JWT via /app/installations/{id}. Anyone who finishes OAuth as themselves can therefore still bind a victim installation_id that is not stored locally yet (webhook not processed or failed, or the Integration row deleted while the GitHub App remains installed). That is the hijack this change is supposed to stop: the attacker's Sentry org gets the victim's installation and repo access. Ownership has to be verified before the integration is created — refuse to continue when the installer cannot be matched, or confirm with GitHub that the OAuth user can access that installation_id — not only in the webhook-already-created branch.

findings.title: Token exchange omits the authorize redirect_uri
findings.body: OAuthLoginView puts redirect_uri on the GitHub authorize redirect, but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749 §4.1.3) requires that same redirect_uri on the token request when it was included in authorization, and GitHub responds with redirect_uri_mismatch or bad_verification_code otherwise. The comment says this follows OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params, which does send redirect_uri. Tests stub https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token to always return an access_token, so they stay green while real installs fail into the generic invalid-installation page.

findings.title: Sender lookup crashes when metadata has no sender
findings.body: Once no OrganizationIntegration exists, the code compares the OAuth login to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only copies sender when pipeline state already has it, and this flow never writes github_authenticated_user into metadata. An ACTIVE Integration without a dict-shaped metadata.sender (older rows, or rows created by this pipeline) raises KeyError or TypeError instead of rendering the installation-failed page. The request 500s, and a missing sender is not treated as a failed authenticity check.

findings.title: Installation-not-found test no longer hits the 404 path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found stubs GET /app/installations/{id} as 404 and previously asserted "The GitHub installation could not be found." It now sends a follow-up setup request with state ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05, while every successful flow in this file uses signature 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3. OAuthLoginView rejects that state before build_integration, and the test only checks for the generic "Invalid installation request." string, so a regression of the 404 handling still passes. Nothing asserts that a mismatched GitHub user is rejected when no Integration row exists yet, which is the branch that skips the new check.
